result.text:
I added repeated commands, the sonar and guarded runs, and `gradle test` passes all 53 tests (the 16 original ones plus 37 new). When I first ran them, 5 new tests failed, but in each case I had worked out the expected result wrong (for example, `g0` turns counter-clockwise 3 times, so the crawler ends up facing Right). The code was right, so I fixed those tests.

## Design
- **Sonar and ground types:** `Sonar` is an interface with `groundAt(Point)`, which returns `FirmSand`, `Silt` or `Boulder`. Each ground type decides for itself what happens when the crawler moves onto it or turns on it, so there are no if-chains on ground type.
  - Moving checks the ground at the cell the crawler is heading to; turning checks the ground it is standing on.
  - Firm sand moves one cell. Silt slides `random.nextInt(10) + 1` cells in the same direction. A boulder raises `"Boulder found"` and leaves the crawler where it was.
  - The facing classes still decide the direction; `moveUp`/`moveDown`/... now all go through one `moveTowards(direction)`.
- **Guarded runs:** the crawler is always in one of two run states, `NormalRun` or `GuardedRun`.
  - Every change of position or facing registers an undo action. `NormalRun` ignores them; `GuardedRun` keeps them in order.
  - `process` has a single `try/catch`: on any error, the current state undoes what it has to, then the exception is rethrown. In `NormalRun` that does nothing; in `GuardedRun` it reverses the recorded moves in reverse order and goes back to `NormalRun`.
  - These errors are raised by the state: `(` inside a guarded run, `)` with no guarded run open, a sequence that ends before its guarded run is closed, and reaching silt during a guarded run.
- **Repetition:** a digit runs the command before it `digit + 2` more times, and only `a`, `t`, `h` and `g` can be repeated. So a digit at the start, a second digit (`a00`), or a digit after `(` or `)` raises `"Invalid command"`.
- **Creating a crawler:** `SurveyCrawler.atFacing(...)` still works and assumes every cell is firm sand. The new `atFacingWithSonar(...)` and `atFacingWithSonarAndRandom(...)` let tests supply their own sonar and a fixed random number.

## Cases the requirements didn't cover, and what I chose
- **Silt in a guarded run:** the crawler actually slides, then raises the error, then undoes the slide. It ends up back where the guarded run started.
- **A `)` with no matching `(`** (e.g. `"a)a"` or `"(a))"`) raises `"Guarded run not started"`.
- **An unclosed guarded run doesn't carry over:** after `"(a"` fails, a following `"a)"` in a new call is still an error.
- **After a failed guarded run, the crawler is back in normal mode:** later errors don't undo anything.
- **An error outside a guarded run** stops processing, and the moves already made stay in place. This includes a boulder in the middle of a repetition like `a9`.
- **Undoing doesn't use the sonar:** it just goes back over cells the crawler already crossed. Also, silt only affects the cell the crawler moves onto, not the cells it slides across.

The new classes are `Sonar`, `Ground`, `FirmSand`, `Silt`, `Boulder`, `CrawlerRunState`, `NormalRun` and `GuardedRun`. I also added `times` and `negated` to `Point`. All new tests are in `SurveyCrawlerTest.java` (test17 to test53).
